messages.content:
Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let all congruences be taken modulo \(397\). Since \(a_0=1\), every \(a_n\) is nonzero, so we may define

\[
b_n \equiv a_n^{-1} \pmod{397}.
\]

From

\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2 \equiv a_n,
\]

multiply by \(b_n b_{n+1}\):

\[
b_n(a_n+1)^2 \equiv b_{n+1}.
\]

Expanding,

\[
b_{n+1} \equiv b_n(a_n^2+2a_n+1)
= (b_n a_n)a_n+2(b_n a_n)+b_n
\equiv a_n+2+b_n.
\]

Thus

\[
a_n \equiv b_{n+1}-b_n-2.
\]

Summing from \(n=0\) to \(2026\),

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n \equiv b_{2027}-b_0-2\cdot 2027.
\]

We have \(b_0=a_0^{-1}=1\). Since \(a_{2026}=9\),

\[
b_{2026}\equiv 9^{-1}.
\]

Now \(9\cdot 44=396\equiv -1\), so \(9^{-1}\equiv -44\equiv 353\). Therefore

\[
b_{2027}\equiv b_{2026}+a_{2026}+2\equiv 353+9+2=364.
\]

Hence

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n \equiv 364-1-4054 \pmod{397}.
\]

Since \(4054\equiv 84\pmod{397}\),

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n \equiv 363-84=279 \pmod{397}.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
